clusters.name: Walter moving the family across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952: within the year, June wrote daily to her sister back home, Walter spent long hours away from her in the orchard, Glen fought at his new school, Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, and the two rowed over money for trees. Her anxiety eased and her functioning rose in September when she joined the church choir, marking where the family settled.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when the late frost took the crop and the bank called in the loan: within the year, Walter drank heavily, he and Glen blamed each other, Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsened, and Nora began wetting the bed in April 1969. Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees by October 1969, marking where the family settled, though he returned to drinking in December 1975 when Glen lost his job.

clusters.name: Glen losing his job at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: within the year, Glen sat out of work most of that year in the truck for hours, he and Marian fought loud fights at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight, she kept to her room and distanced from her mother, and Glen started the delivery truck job in March 1976. Nora's functioning rose in June 1976 when she began eating again and made the track team, marking where the family settled.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma moving into Nora and Hollis's house in January 1990 after selling her farm: within the year, Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, Hollis worked late and kept out of the rows, he took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, Nora's eczema flared on both hands, and she and Hollis rowed most nights. Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991, and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, marking where the family settled.
